_comment: A PC takes two floppy drives with independent swap lists, a CD-ROM, and up
to two hard disks. Following the DOSBox-X core: the hard disk slot's file
SEEDS a writable image rather than being written in place, and what comes
back out is the whole disk, byte for byte, so it can be handed straight
back into this slot to carry on from.
There is deliberately no slot for a PCem .cfg: the machine is composed from
settings, and letting a user paste in a config would reintroduce exactly the

slots.title: Floppy disks (drive A:)
slots.help: Disk images for drive A:. The first is in the drive when the machine starts, and the order here is the order they are swapped in. The drive itself is chosen with the Floppy Drive A setting. Its default is Auto, which chooses the drive that fits the image you give here. If you choose a drive yourself, make sure it matches. PCem does not refuse a disk that the drive cannot read completely. It stops the head at the drive's last track, and the machine gets read errors.

slots.title: Floppy disks (drive B:)
slots.help: Disk images for drive B:. It works the same way as drive A:. A machine with only one drive ignores this.

slots.title: CD-ROMs
slots.help: Discs for the CD-ROM drive. PCem reads the image itself, so a .cue file with its track files beside it works. It needs a machine with a CD-ROM controller. The CD-ROM settings appear once a disc is given here.

slots.title: Hard disk (C:)
slots.help: A hard disk image, used as drive C:. Your file is never changed. The machine works on a copy of it that can be written to. What is written stays for the session, is part of savestates, and can be exported as save data. An exported image can be given here to continue from it. The disk's geometry is worked out from the file unless the Hard Disk settings say otherwise.

slots.title: Second hard disk (D:)
slots.help: A second hard disk. It works the same way.
